title: SigSel: A MATLAB package for high-resolution mass spectrometry signals
author: Pérez-López, Ginebreda, et al.

steps.title: Load datasets into MATLAB
steps.instruction: Import the charge‑filtered LC‑MS datasets into the MATLAB computing environment so they are ready for ROI compression and MCR‑ALS analysis.

steps.title: Apply ROI compression to samples
steps.instruction: Compress and filter the data using the ROI concept, selecting MS‑ROIs based on three parameters – background‑noise intensity threshold, instrument mass accuracy, and the minimum number of m/z signals that define an elution peak at the chromatographic resolution. Apply this ROI procedure simultaneously to all four metabolomics samples, producing a column‑wise augmented data matrix with 290 columns (one for each selected MS‑ROI) and a number of rows equal to the total number of MS scans (retention times) across the LC runs of all samples.

steps.title: Run MCR‑ALS decomposition
steps.instruction: Perform bilinear factor decomposition of the MS‑ROI matrix with the MCR‑ALS algorithm using 30 components, which explains 99.33 % of the total data variance. Confirm that increasing the number of components does not reveal additional chemical information (extra components correspond only to background noise). Identify components that originate from solvent, background, or instrumental noise and later filter these non‑sample‑related components using the visualization and filtering tools available in SigSel.

substeps.instruction: Set the number of MCR‑ALS components to 30.
Run the MCR‑ALS algorithm and record the explained variance (99.33 %).
Inspect additional components; if they represent only noise, do not increase the component count.
Use SigSel to visualize each component’s spectra and elution profile.
Filter out components identified as solvent, background, or instrumental noise.
